title: Jesse Boot's Advert for 128 Cheaper Medicines, March 1877
conflicts: Growth after the March 1877 advert: the University of Nottingham archive note says profits doubled within a month, Spartacus says takings doubled; the story attributes 'profits doubled' to the archive. The £100 a week by autumn 1877 is 'turnover' in Judy Slinn's company history and 'takings' in Boots plc's account quoted by Picture Nottingham; the story attributes it to Slinn as turnover. King's Lynn History dates a 128-item advert series to February 1871, against the archive's 12 March 1877; the story follows the archive. Partnership dated 1870 (Boots) or c.1871 (Grace's); story says 'around 1870'. The date of the move to 16-20 Goose Gate (1877 per the Boots newsroom, 1881 per Grace's Guide) is left out.
notes: Arc changed from founding-decision to change-of-direction: the episode is the family herbalist shop's turn to cut-price branded medicines. Quote stance: challenges (Socrates on the cook beating the physician when untrained buyers judge). The University of Nottingham PDF loads but its text is compressed, so the checker marks it live without naming Boots; seven other sources are OK.
